meta.notes: All coordinates are in TILE units unless a field name ends in _px. Rows count from top (0) down. Ground band is rows 15-17. 'gx' = grid x, 'gy' = grid y, 'w'/'h' in tiles. Player hitbox is 28x44px; spawn places feet on the given tile top. The typed shape of this file is src/data/levels.ts.
meta.structure: Every screen with an obstacle on it carries an ANSR badge, placed early on the walking path so it can be taken BEFORE the obstacles it answers. Head Office is the exception and carries none (owner call): a badge whose effect is deliberately unassigned taught the player that taking one does nothing, one screen before the one that saves them. The badge is not a static tile: it levitates along a straight vertical line through a band around its anchor (POWERUPS.FLOAT_AMPLITUDE / FLOAT_PERIOD), riding up to just below the ceiling and back down to a height a jump can reach - never low enough to be walked into, which is what makes taking it a decision rather than a formality. Taking it is what makes the rest of the screen safe; missing it is what the delay log is for. One screen delivers its badge instead of hanging it up: on Hire Under Fire a drone drops it onto a floating brick and it expires (badge.delivery = airdrop, badge.restGy), so there the instruction is 'get there in time AND jump for it'.
meta.clock: monthsBase is booked on clearing a screen. The six bases sum to JOURNEY.ANSR_BENCHMARK_MONTHS, so a clean assisted run lands exactly on ANSR's published benchmark. Every obstacle costs one life and adds JOURNEY.SETBACK_MONTHS to the clock, capped at JOURNEY.MAX_MONTHS.

conventions.solid: static collidable platform/wall (non-lethal). Walking into a wall stops you.
conventions.spawn: player entry point (feet), always near far-left
conventions.exit: reaching this x (right edge trigger) advances to next screen
conventions.badge: ANSR capability pickup; anchored early in the screen and levitating vertically around gy (see POWERUPS in tuning.config.ts for how the band is derived). On a rail the mark starts at the MIDDLE of the band, rises to the top and then comes down (owner call), which makes it a pickup you stop for rather than one you take on the way past - see badgeFloat.ts and docs/OPEN.md. 'delivery' switches that off: with "airdrop" (Hire Under Fire only, owner call) the badge is not on a rail at all - a flying ANSR supply drone crosses the screen along row 'gy', releases it over one of the 'drops' columns in turn, and the badge comes to rest on the floating brick at row 'restGy' there for POWERUPS.DROP.LIFETIME seconds before it is gone (omit 'restGy' and it rests on the floor). Miss it and the next drone comes with the next column, so the screen is never unanswerable; stand still and you get nothing, which is the point on the one screen where standing still is how you get burnt. 'gx'/'gy' are still authored because everything structural reads them: gx is the column the badge belongs to for the badge-before-obstacle rule, and gy is the drone's flight row. With "perch" (Compliance) the mark simply stands on the top course of a floating brick deck at 'gx'/'restGy'. With "ceiling" (the Workplace, owner call) it hangs in the beam of a ceiling spotlight at 'gx'/'gy', drops straight down onto the floating cabinet at 'restGy' after POWERUPS.CEILING.HOLD seconds, rests there for LIFETIME and is gone until the next cycle - the only delivery that is visible before it is takeable.
conventions.pedestal: a solid with role "pedestal" is a floating block, drawn as its screen's own prop rather than as level material (on Hire Under Fire, the single brick the badge is dropped onto). It is real geometry - it collides, it can be landed on, and the physics validator has to prove the badge on top of it is reachable - and it replaced the old "hurdle" role, which was a one-tile step in the middle of the same screen and was removed (owner call: it added nothing to a boss screen). A pedestal has to leave the corridor under it walkable: at row 12 its underside is 36px clear of a standing head.
conventions.dragons: the hiring dragon on Hire Under Fire - the screen's only obstacle, and it wears glasses and nothing else (owner call: no jacket and no tie). Exactly one is authored; it is a list because every other hazard family here is one. 'from'/'to' are the columns of the ground it STANDS ON at the far end of the screen - on two feet, so there is no hover row to author: its height comes from HAZARDS.DRAGON.BODY_H and the ground band. Its BODY IS NOT A HITBOX: the only lethal thing on the screen is one straight, growing, slightly diverging cone of fire thrown from its jaw along the floor in front of it, so nothing can cost a life without a telegraph in front of it and nothing on the screen travels. It opens every attempt with a roar it cannot attack during (HAZARDS.DRAGON.ROAR_TIME), which is the guaranteed safe beat the level starts on. 'seed' picks its rhythm without Math.random, and 'taunts' are the strings painted on the burst's own plaque, one per burst - drawn content, so uppercase and apostrophe-free, and NOT stripped from the bundle.
conventions.monsters: a compliance monster patrolling one corridor of the Compliance maze. 'from'/'to' are the grid columns it may wander between and 'gy' is the surface row it stands on at 'from'; 'slope' (-1 rising to the right, 0 flat, 1 falling) steps that row per tread and 'slopeRun' is how many columns make up one tread (default 1, and 2 on this screen's flights), so a monster can walk a staircase without ever standing half a row inside it. Its name is drawn on a framed plaque above it and is the ONLY signage on the screen - the five names are the five filings, so a second copy of them on boards in the sky is a duller label layer competing with this one (owner call, twice). It re-rolls direction and speed at every junction from its own seeded generator - unpredictable, never hunting. Touch one unassisted and the stage stalls. 'route' is the way home once the badge is taken: a list of surface cells it walks through, corner by corner, to reach the gather cell - the monsters use the player's own staircases rather than drifting through the geometry, which is the whole point of the picture.
conventions.lift: a moving platform. 'gx'/'gy'/'w' are where it PARKS (top of the plate at gy) and 'toGy' the row whose top it descends to. It carries the player down while they stand on it and returns when they step off. It is not in 'solids' on purpose: it moves, so the hazard owns the live box and nothing derives its position twice.
conventions.mummies: the figure wrapped in caution tape on the Workplace screen. 'from'/'to' are the grid columns it walks between and 'gy' the surface row it stands on. Unlike a compliance monster it NEVER turns around: it trudges from 'from' to 'to' at one constant speed and then loops straight back to 'from', so its path is a metronome the player can read from the far side of the frame rather than a chase. Touch it while it is still wrapped and the stage stalls. Three hits from the badge's cutter strip its three tape layers.
conventions.terminal: the sparking computer terminal on the Workplace screen: where the freed colleague runs to, and the thing whose success chime clears the tape, the signs and the dark. Decoration until then - it is not in 'solids' and never collides.
conventions.clutter: the Workplace screen's floor dressing, authored here because it is layout: 'barricade' is the striped under-construction trestle with its hazard lamp, 'cone' a traffic cone, 'sign' a wet floor sign, 'ladder' a step ladder somebody abandoned and 'post' a tape stand. THREE stretches of floor are kept clear and all three are load-bearing. Columns 9-13 are where the wrapped figure starts every sweep, and with a ladder and a tape run standing there he was unreadable in the one place the player has to read him from. Columns 23-25 are the terminal: it is the thing the freed colleague runs to and the only readout of the win, and a cone and a ladder authored on top of it buried it completely - the tape run from post 22 to post 27 crosses in front of it at head height instead, which is the picture (the fix itself taped off). And nothing stands next to the ceiling stain at column 12, because a bucket needs clear floor to be seen at all. Posts are authored in PAIRS and the tape is strung within a pair, never from one pair to the next - stringing it post to post drew one unbroken yellow line from wall to wall, which read as a wire across the picture rather than as taped-off stretches of floor. None of it collides (the partition is the only jump on the screen) and all of it is cleared by the fix, which is the point: the room is uninhabitable until somebody puts it right.
conventions.gather: where the monsters walk to once the badge is taken - they stop scowling and cross the maze to this cell together, which is the moment the screen is built around
conventions.zone: kept as authoring metadata only - it records which obstacles were written as the felt problem and which as the relief. It no longer describes a position, because the badge now sits ahead of both.

screens.name: Head Office
screens.note: Head Office has NO BADGE (owner call). It carried a SAFE_PASSAGE mark as a tutorial - collect it and nothing happens - and that is exactly why it went: the first ANSR badge a player ever sees taught them that taking one changes nothing, one screen before the badge that saves their life. The first mark in the run is now 1Wrk on Setup Delays, where taking it is the difference between walking through the DENIED stamps and being flattened by them. The three labelled steps are the tutorial: they teach the jump, and they are the only thing on this screen that has to be learnt.

solids.note: One course of brick between the two stamps of a pair (owner call), so crossing a pair is a jump as well as a piece of timing. One tile: 40px against a 140px jump, i.e. a hop the player takes in his stride. The column is the MIDPOINT of the pair (7 and 12 -> 10) and that is the whole constraint: a player pinned against the left face of this block stands at x 372-400, and the stamps either side of it press 252-348 and 460-556, so waiting at the wall is never inside a stamp. At gx 9 it would be.

The same hop between the second pair (20 and 25). gx 23 rather than the exact midpoint 22: at gx 22 a player pinned against it stands at 852-880 and the gx 20 stamp presses 772-868, so the resting place would be under a stamp.

badge.note: 1Wrk stands the setup up properly, so the approvals stop coming back DENIED. Taken at the top of the screen, before the first pair of stamps. This is the LAST RAIL BADGE in the game, and its mark starts mid-rail and rises (owner call), so it is out of reach when a running player passes this column and has to be waited for: stand under gx 4 and jump when it comes back down. Do not treat it as a hop taken in stride. With it the whole mechanism runs at ASSIST_TIME_SCALE - wide windows you can walk through - and a stamp that touches an ANSR-backed player cannot press: it retracts from where it touched. Without it, being under a stamp when it lands flattens you.

screens.name: Compliance
screens.note: Owner rebuild, authored from the owner's reference sketch, re-cut once because the first pass got the STAIRS wrong, and re-cut a third time on the owner's pass that deleted the badge rail and the long brown platform. The screen is a STAIRCASE MAZE: no route along the ground, so the exit is only reachable by climbing. Read bottom-left to right: the ANSR mark stands on a FLOATING brick structure, and getting to it is TWO jumps in OPPOSITE directions (owner call, third note on this screen): running right, jump onto 'step-ansr-approach' (gx 4-6, gy 12, 120px over the corridor), then turn around and jump back up-LEFT onto 'wall-ansr-mark' (gx 1-2, gy 9), which is 120px higher again and 40px across a gap - the mark sits on its right-hand column. Walk under both and you keep going with no GCC-BOT, which is the point: the mark used to hang on a levitating rail, then stood on the floor where nobody could avoid it, then sat one hop off the ground where everybody took it on the way past; the left corridor runs on to the lower staircase, which rises onto the filings block; back down to the top tread (stair-tds, gx 15) and one hop LEFT onto the clearance HOIST, which carries the player up two rows to the upper stairs, the top gallery and the statutory wall; the wall's top is the jumping-off point for the clearance LIFT down into the far bay and the exit. Every level is a corridor with a wandering monster on it, so the maze cannot be crossed by holding one direction on one level. Take GCC-BOT and every toll gate stands open for good, the five monsters stop scowling and cross the maze to the block, and the weather clears. WHAT CHANGED ON THIS RE-CUT, and why it matters if this is ever edited again: the long 'platform-registers' (gx 9-14, gy 8) is GONE and the HOIST stands in its place, because the owner asked for a plate that goes up and down instead of a slab you had to jump up-left onto from 120px below. The hoist parks at gy 9 and NOT one row lower: its underside at 376 has to leave 84px of headroom over the highest tread beneath its span (stair-gst at gy 12, top 480), or a player on that tread can no longer hop up to stair-tds and the maze becomes uncompletable - and nothing in the static-solid validator would catch it, because the plate is not a solid in this file. 'wall-hoist-guide' at gx 8 is the owner's left-hand wall, and lifting the badge structure into the air made it load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces: from the structure's deck at 480 the apex is feet-340, which is ABOVE the plate's parked top at 360 and only 80px away horizontally, so without the pier the whole lower maze could be skipped by jumping structure -> plate -> upper flight. The staircases stay ONE TILE THICK with open sky under them and TWO-column treads; step-resubmit at gx16 gy13 is the only way out of the strip under the lower flight. The block is 7x5 and still runs all the way to the statutory wall on purpose: shortening it opens a strip of ground that can only be entered by falling and cannot be left.

hoist.note: The clearance hoist - the owner's replacement for the long brown platform that used to stand at gy 8 ('make this a floating platform like the yellow one on the other side but make it go up and down'). Same machine as the lift and the same rule: it moves only while the player is on it (UP, here) and returns only while it is empty, so it can never rise into a body it is not carrying. It PARKS low (gy 9) and travels to gy 7, where its right edge sits 40px from stair-transfer-pricing at the same height - board it with one hop left off stair-tds and you are on the upper flight. Not in solids for the same reason the lift is not: it moves, so the hazard owns its live box and this file says only where it parks.

lift.note: The clearance lift, and the one thing on the screen that is not stone: it is the yellow plate in the sketch with the arrow pointing down. Step off the top of the statutory wall onto it and it takes you down to the floor of the far bay; step off and it goes back up for the next time. Deliberately NOT listed in solids - it moves, so the hazard owns it and there is exactly one source for its position (levels.json holds where it parks, not where it is).

monsters.name: LEGAL
monsters.note: LEGAL rides the clearance hoist, which is this maze's fifth level now that the long platform at gy 8 is gone. `hoist` means its surface is the plate's live top rather than a row in this file, so `gy` here is only the plate's parking row - the corridor it wanders is the plate's own span (gx 9-14). Boarding the hoist therefore costs the same as any other corridor on this screen: you read the monster first.

badge.note: GCC-BOT files on your behalf. Every toll gate in the maze stands open for good, the five compliance monsters stop scowling and walk off to the landing together, and the weather over the market clears - the whole maze becomes a staircase you simply climb. Skip it and the same maze has to be timed corridor by corridor, with a wandering monster on every level. DELIVERY: this is the one badge that is neither on a rail nor air-dropped (owner call: 'remove the ANSR powerup rail and instead make a brick wall which will have an ANSR powerup on it'). It stands on the top course of 'wall-ansr-mark', which is a FLOATING brick structure over the left corridor and not a wall standing on the floor (owner call, a second note on the same pass: 'the powerup is easily available and is on the way, so the player would anyway take it - keep it somewhere that it is on the user to take it or not, maybe a floating brick structure where it resides, the player jumps up to it, takes it and then comes back to the normal path'). On the ground it was a hurdle you had to clear anyway, so everybody collected the mark for free; floating at gy 12 its underside leaves 36px of air over a standing head, so holding RIGHT walks straight underneath and the detour is a decision. The mark is CENTRED on the deck (owner call: 'the ANSR powerup is on the right side of the brick, make it centre on the floating brick'), which is what 'restW': 2 means - gx is the deck's first column and the one-tile pickup is centred across the two, at x 60-100. It used to stand on the deck's LAST column under an older owner rule (a mark in the middle can be walked off the far side by somebody who landed late), and that rule was written for a deck you arrive at walking RIGHT; this one is reached by turning round and jumping back up-LEFT, so the player arrives at its far end and walks into the middle regardless. gx 6 is still the last column any part of this pickup may use, because TAX's corridor starts at gx 7 and the badge has to precede every obstacle. The deck is THREE blocks (gx 4-6) rather than four, and that is a measured number, not a shape: it is 120px over the floor, so it has to be cleared in one arc, and every column added to its LEFT end costs run-up. At gx 3-6 a one-tap auto-run player had a 0.20s window of taps that landed on it; at gx 4-6 the window is 0.35s, against a 0.30s budget (badgeReach.test.ts).

screens.name: Workplace
screens.note: Owner-specified replacement for Local Expertise, and it sits here - straight after Compliance - because a workplace is the first thing you actually walk into once the filings clear. The picture: a broken office. Lights flickering, wet floor signs, caution tape over everything, and one figure mummified in three layers of RED barrier tape trudging the floor - a different colour from the room's caution yellow on purpose, because a wrapped man in the same yellow as nine props merged into the set. He paces his corridor TO AND FRO (see 'mummies'), pausing to turn at each end, so he is a metronome rather than a chase: read one leg and pick your moment. He used to loop instead, snapping back to his start column, and the owner replaced that because a body that vanishes at one end and reappears at the other reads as a respawn rather than as a person. AND HE THROWS (owner call: 'add a capability for the mummy to throw the bandages at the player capturing him'): every HAZARDS.WORKPLACE.THROW_INTERVAL he stops, raises a coil of his own tape over his shoulder for THROW_WINDUP, and unwinds it down the floor at the player's shins. Contact books the same 'mummy' delay as his body does and the player is shown wrapped where he stood, which is what 'capturing him' looks like. The answer is to jump it - the roll flies 30px above the floor line so clearing it costs 41px of a 140px jump - and the three numbers that keep that fair are the long telegraph, the fact that he stands still through the whole throw (so every attempt costs him ground), and that only one roll is ever in the air. He will not throw at a player closer than THROW_MIN_RANGE, because a roll spawned inside the player is a hit with no telegraph; inside that distance his body is the threat, which is the fight this screen was already about. The player spawns behind the partition at gx 7, which is two clear columns short of the corridor, so he is out of reach on frame one - that partition is both the safety and this screen's one jump, and now that the figure throws it is a place to READ him from rather than a place to wait behind. The gap between the partition and the corridor is not spare space: it is where you stand to burn the tape off him, and it is why the orb never has to cross the partition to reach him. Unassisted the screen is still winnable, but waiting him out no longer works now that he comes back: the move is to meet him head on and JUMP him. That is measured, not assumed - a jump clears his 78px crown for 0.455s, the head-on closing speed is 260 + 150 = 410 px/s so the 88px of overlap take 0.21s, and overtaking him from behind needs 0.8s of air, which is impossible on purpose and is what stops 'hold right' being an answer. With the badge you do not dodge him at all - you free him.

badge.note: DELIVERY: the rail is gone (owner call: 'for the powerup remove the rail and add - from the spot light I just said - an ANSR powerup that falls and stays for a few seconds, and the user has to take it otherwise it's gone, and this happens at regular intervals; and this powerup doesn't drop immediately, it's visible as the user comes to this screen but drops after a few seconds the user has spent in the screen, and this drops on a cabinet or something which is before the partition wall so the user can take it safely but the player has to put in some effort to grab it'). So this is the fourth delivery model and the only one tied to its own screen's picture: the mark hangs in the beam of the FIRST of the four ceiling spotlights - gx 5 is that fitting's own centre column (x 220), so it falls straight down its own axis - waits POWERUPS.CEILING.HOLD (3.2s) while the player walks in and watches it, drops onto the top of the floating overhead cabinet at restGy 12, rests there for LIFETIME (4.5s) and is gone until the next cycle. The cabinet ('cabinet-badge', gx 4-5 gy 12) is the effort: it FLOATS, leaving 36px over a standing head, so holding RIGHT walks straight underneath and takes nothing, and getting on top of it means clearing 120px of the 140 a jump has - i.e. the button held for ~20 frames, the same figure the air-dropped brick on screen 4 forced. It is BEFORE the partition (gx 7) so the whole transaction happens on the safe side of the wall, which is the owner's 'so the user can take it safely'; and its right edge (x 240) is 40px clear of the wall's face, which is load-bearing rather than tidy - a player pinned against the partition must not be standing UNDER the cabinet, or its underside caps his jump at 36px and the screen is sealed. The only badge in the game that is visible before it is takeable: the offer is on screen from frame one and being ready for it is a decision. The rest is unchanged - it is still the only badge that hands the player a verb of their own: it makes a cutter appear and the shoot button live, and what it fires are small orbs of fire. Three hits BURN the three tape layers off him - an ember front eats along each band, ash falls away, and a permanent soot mark is left behind, so the body carries the score rather than only the three pips over his head - and then he unravels, and he does NOT die. He is a colleague somebody taped off like a piece of broken furniture: shirt, sleeves rolled up, straight to the sparking terminal, and it is his work that lights the floor and clears every sign and every strip of tape. The blocker becomes the person who makes it right. Skip the badge and there is no cutter, so the same figure has to be timed and jumped instead.

solids.note: THE floating brick the drone drops the badge onto - there is exactly ONE now (owner call: 'remove the 3 brick structures where the ANSR powerup drops, remove the 2 and just keep 1'). One tile square, at row 12: its underside is y=520 against a standing head at y=556, so the corridor still walks clear underneath it, and its top at y=480 puts the badge's box 76px above that head - a jump of 76 against 140 available. Moved closer to spawn (gx 10, spawn is at gx 1) for better accessibility early in the screen.

dragons.name: HIRING AT SCALE
dragons.note: It STANDS ON THE GROUND on two feet (owner call, third pass - it used to hover over row 9, and before that it roamed the whole frame holding a standoff from the player). There is no hover row here any more: HAZARDS.DRAGON.BODY_H and the ground band decide its height, and columns 23-29 are the patch of floor it holds, drifting only inside HAZARDS.DRAGON.ROOST_DRIFT of the centre of them. Its BODY IS NOT A HITBOX: the only lethal thing on the screen is one straight, growing, slightly diverging CONE of fire thrown from its jaw down the lane in front of it (HAZARDS.DRAGON.CONE_*). Nothing travels - the fireballs and the rolling flame fronts are gone - so the dangerous floor is a fixed strip with a rhythm, telegraphed for BURST_WINDUP along the ground before it lights. Each burst carries ONE of the taunts on a plaque that stays put over the lane; the next burst brings the next one. The taunts are drawn content rather than notes: uppercase only, no apostrophes, short enough to read while the floor in front of you is on fire.

badge.note: The one badge that is DELIVERED (owner call): no levitating rail on this screen. An ANSR supply drone crosses row 5 and drops the badge over ONE column - gx10 (moved closer to spawn for better accessibility, spawn is at gx1, previously gx16) - and it lands on a FLOATING BRICK at row 12 rather than on the floor (owner call, second pass), so taking it is a jump as well as a journey. It lies up there for POWERUPS.DROP.LIFETIME seconds and then it is gone, and the next drone brings another one to the same brick. Talent500 then does two things at once: a teal halo makes the fire harmless, and the same badge puts a water cannon in the player's hands. Water beats the fire first - jets crossing the burning cone cut the burst short - and only between bursts does a jet reach the dragon and take a hit off the one thing it is wearing. Four hits and the glasses wash off, the beast TOPPLES to the floor, its costume unzips down one side and the five candidates who were inside it walk out one by one stamped HIRED, and the empty suit lies there and then vanishes (HAZARDS.DRAGON.COSTUME_*): the screen is won on a hire rather than on a kill, and the environment comes good with them (Dragon.relief). Skip every drop and the dragon cannot be answered at all: the stage is a dodge from the spawn to the exit.

screens.name: ANSR Tech Park
screens.note: The Tech Park has NO BADGE (owner call: 'remove the ANSR powerup badge and rail from the ANSR Tech Park screen'), and it is the SECOND screen to lose one for the same reason Head Office did. It carried a SAFE_PASSAGE mark - a levitating rail with an effect deliberately left unassigned - on the reasoning that the ANSR mark belongs on every screen. But this is the arrival: the run is already won, the receipt is the next thing the player sees, and a pickup that does nothing on the one screen with nothing to defend against is a rail hanging in the middle of the payoff. With Head Office's gone too, every badge left in the game is a capability that changes the screen it is on, and 'a badge is help you chose to take' has no exceptions. SAFE_PASSAGE is deleted outright - the type, its COPY line and the validator's allowance for it - because a badge type no screen carries is the next session's confusion.
